prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form, which made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize on B012 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. I re-tested it after reading all six round-1 files and the chair's questions, and the case holds on the science. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and incretin action in humans, Drucker defined proglucagon-derived peptide biology and its actions, and Mojsov identified the bioactive 7-36 form. The resulting drug class is confirmed in many independent randomized outcome trials, with glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal benefit. Maturity is not in question, and the clinical scale makes delay hard to defend. Because every member names the same three laureates, I take the chair's point that round 2 should test the weak points instead of repeating the agreement. A single part also avoids splitting a three-person ceiling across two achievements, which would leave each part under-credited.
statement.case_against: Credit remains the weak point and I do not think it can be fully resolved from the files. Mojsov's priority relative to Habener and colleagues cannot be verified by me, and Habener is absent from the supplied names. Knudsen's protraction chemistry is what turned a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a medicine, so the citation risks reading as if the discoverers made the drugs. If the committee concluded that Mojsov's independent contribution is weaker than the record suggests, I would reopen the third name instead of defending her by default. I would not add a fourth name, and I would not accept a configuration that drops Holst or Drucker to include Knudsen.

responses.point: Perlmann would not accept a configuration that includes Knudsen at the expense of the basic-science names, and treats the exclusion as defensible only if stated openly.
responses.response: I agree with the principle and with the openness requirement, and I would put it into the citation text itself. My citation names the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form, and says that these discoveries made the therapies possible. It does not say the laureates made the drugs. That wording credits what the three did and leaves the engineering of long-acting agonists to the record. I part from you slightly on how comfortable I am. The exclusion of Knudsen is a real cost, and I would accept it only because the three-name ceiling forces a choice and the physiology precedes the pharmacology.

responses.point: Sandberg says he would reopen the Knudsen question if Mojsov's priority proves weaker than the record suggests, and ranks B024 as the strongest mechanistic alternative.
responses.response: I share the conditional. The files give us no evidence that settles Mojsov versus Habener, so the question is whether a configuration with her is still defensible when it cannot be settled. I think it is: her synthesis and characterisation of the active peptide is documented independently of the priority dispute. I would not swap in Knudsen in that case; I would prefer to keep the citation about the physiology and active form and acknowledge the dispute in the committee's own record. On B024 I still regard Walter and Mori as the cleanest pair on the list, but I stay with a single part this year because the three-person limit would force a split of B012 that I consider worse.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius keeps TNF blockade (B046) as an alternative and moved toward the two-name June and Sadelain version of B009, noting TNF has more than twenty years of independent confirmation.
responses.response: The twenty years of confirmation is a fair point against my treatment of CAR-T as less mature, and I accept that B046 is the more settled of the two on durability. I still keep B009 ahead as an alternative, because the CAR-T concept has changed treatment of B-cell malignancies in a way that is specific to engineered cells, whereas for B046 I am unsure that the credited pair's step is the decisive one rather than the antibodies and fusion proteins others built. I do agree with your move to the two-name version: Rosenberg's adoptive transfer is a distinct strand, and I have moved my own view in that direction. Eshhar remains unresolved either way, which is why I would not take B009 as a second part now.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, asks whether B024 or B009 can serve as a second part and whether B016 is a class-defining paradigm.
responses.response: On your second-part question, I do not think B009 is ready because Eshhar and Rosenberg are unresolved, and B024 is clean but its disease payoff is still prospective. Together with the three-name ceiling, that leaves GLP-1 alone as my answer. On B016, I would put the deciding element in the target biology: the BCR-ABL oncogene discovery sits outside Druker, Lydon and Sawyers, so I treat it as a strong candidate for a later year, not this one.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active peptide can be adequately established relative to Habener, which I cannot verify from the supplied files.
How openly the citation should state that long-acting agonist development (Knudsen) is not what the prize rewards, and whether the wording I propose is enough.
Whether a clinically anchored second part would be preferable to a single part if the committee found a way to fit it within three people.
For B009, whether a two-name June and Sadelain version can address Eshhar and Rosenberg adequately.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. No shortlisted candidate matches my research directly. I co-authored the 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper and have co-authored several papers with Rickard Sandberg, but none of these relate to a shortlisted discovery or credited name. No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted ballots.
